newsitem.title: TAIWAN: CHINESE BUYERS SIDELINED, AWAIT USDA REPORT.
newsitem.headline: CHINESE BUYERS SIDELINED, AWAIT USDA REPORT.

text.p: Chinese oilseed buyers were sidelined and will wait for the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) crop report before deciding on their next move, traders said on Monday.
"Chinese buyers are waiting for the USDA report on Tuesday," a U.S. trader in China said. "Buyers may buy some supplies if the market can show some clear direction after the USDA report."
A trader said price-sensitive Chinese buyers are waiting mainly for CBOT soybean prices to ease.
"There needs to be a good price to lure Chinese buyers back to the soybean market," she said.
Buyers are willing to buy soybean at US$260 per tonne C&F and soymeal at $265 a tonne C&F, the trader added.
"Someone bought some U.S. soybeans earlier at $260, so other buyers don't want to buy at higher prices," she said. U.S. soybeans were being quoted at $270 to $275 a tonne C&F.
Chinese traders said weather conditions in growing areas in the U.S. and tight supplies on nearby months were the key factors for the soybean market.
China is unlikely to import corn this year due to ample government corn stocks, traders said.
